title: Geography of the district and the bell system
summary: He maps the area he was allowed to go in, describes cribs and apartment houses, and explains the bell-ring system for picking up orders.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: You see? Well do you remember, was there a place, Turo's, that had lunches or something? Food, was that a restaurant? Do you remember that? Turo's. I think that was at Conti, wasn't it? Turo's. Bienville, I guess. They called it Bienville and Basin.
Oh, I never had much contact.
You never got up in there.
I thought you might have gone there.
No, like Tom Anderson and that place. I never got up Tom Anderson's?
No. You never got up Tom Anderson's?

No. I never got that far. The farthest I went was to Franklin, back to Robinson. Yeah. And from, I'd say from St. Louis to Iberville. That was the first, that was our locale, you know, because they didn't allow you to go around in front of them houses.
Were there many of the good houses back there, away from Basin Street, back in the-

No, the good houses mostly out there. On Basin. Around Basin Street. And they had a few on the other side of Ramport Street. Yeah. Between Ramport and Burgundy. I used to have a few around there. On there too.
Were they mostly cribs then, just the individual?

Well, no, all the cribs was this side, but them was mostly apartment houses like, you know. Well, people lived in there then. Oh yeah, they lived in there, but those prostitutes, you know. Yeah. Well, they lived in there and that's where they did all their business, right out there.

So the first we was allowed to go was to Franklin, back to Robeson and from Iberville down to St. Louis. Well, from St. Louis, on St. Louis Street, that was running from Robeson to Liberty. Yeah. See, because the cemetery was running from Liberty to Basin. Yeah. And the other cemetery was running from Robeson to Claiborne. You see, they're known up Claiborne to Iberville. Yeah. But the house was on that side from the cemetery.

We used to catch a lot of artists around there, you know. We used to work by bells. See, not by phone, we used to work by bells. They had a bell in every house, you know, and they'd give so many rings for a citizen of the street because it would register up on the wall, you know. Just where we had to go to pick up the artists. It was easy, it was simple to catch on to. I was always apt to catch on to anything fast, you know. Uh-huh. In a week's time, I had everything down pat.
Wasn't no trouble for me at all. All I had to do in that bell ring, come in and look up at that number. I know what locale I had to go to.
